title: MakeItBeauty kit component (v0)
description: A parameterized design fragment, referenced from designs as "kit/{id}". Nodes are design-schema nodes positioned relative to the frame; {{props.*}} slots resolve with the standard template engine; computed entries map a numeric prop linearly onto node geometry (prop × scale, clamped). Nested instance nodes are not allowed (v0). Three variants (see allOf): declarative (default — nodes required, they ARE the component; no code execution ever), native (native: true + dataFields — a TRUSTED generator inside the renderer produces the render nodes from (props, data, frame); official kit only, community publish validation rejects it; declared nodes are only the static palette preview, so [] or absent is fine), and code (kind: "code" + code — architecture.md §7.6: a pure render({props, frame}) => nodes function executed in the capability-less QuickJS sandbox; declared nodes are only the static palette preview; computed is declarative-only and forbidden here — compute geometry inside render(); native/dataFields/dataConnector are mutually exclusive with kind "code"). Code components are the one variant open to the community registry alongside declarative ones. This file is the contract for packages/kit/components.

id.description: Component id; instances reference it as "kit/{id}".

kind.description: Component variant. Absent means "declarative" (the original format — every pre-existing file stays valid). "code" (§7.6): the `code` source is REQUIRED and executes in the capability-less sandbox as render({props, frame}) => text/rect/image nodes; declared nodes become the OPTIONAL static palette preview ([] or absent is fine); computed is forbidden (declarative-only — code computes its own geometry); native/dataFields/dataConnector are forbidden (mutually exclusive — a component is trusted-native or sandboxed-code, never both).

code.description: kind "code" only (forbidden otherwise): JavaScript source that defines render — `function render({ props, frame }) { ... }` or `const render = ({ props, frame }) => ...` — returning an array of design-schema text/rect/image nodes in frame coordinates. Executed in the capability-less QuickJS-in-WASM sandbox under hard limits (~50ms CPU, 32MB memory, ≤512 nodes, ≤512KB output; source ≤64KB — this maxLength mirrors the sandbox's byte cap). Deterministic by construction: no Date, no Math.random, no async, no host APIs; publish executes it twice against the declared prop defaults and byte-compares the output. Output nodes flow through the exact same validation/scale/offset/sanitize gates as declarative fragments.

category.description: Optional palette-menu category, a lowercase slug. The editor groups components under it and treats uncategorized components as a catch-all bucket. Recommended taxonomy (official kit uses exactly these): cards (framed containers/showcases), stats (single-number metrics and meters), data (array-driven connector visuals), banners (wide text/header strips), decor (dividers and ornaments).

frame.description: The component's own coordinate space. Expansion uniform-scales it into the instance box by s = min(instance.w/frame.w, instance.h/frame.h), top-left aligned.

props.description: Declared slots. Instance props merge over these defaults; {{props.name}} placeholders in nodes resolve to the merged values.

nodes.description: Design-schema fragment, positioned relative to the frame — (0,0) is the component's own top-left corner. Required (min 1) for declarative components; for native and code components it is only the static palette preview and may be [] or absent (see allOf).

native.description: Official-kit only: the renderer produces this component's nodes with a trusted generator from (props, data, frame) — array-driven visuals (heatmap cells, language bars) that declarative fragments cannot express. The data the generator sees is the snapshot subtree of the component's dataConnector (default github). The declared nodes remain as the static fallback/palette preview. Community publish validation rejects this flag; declaring it requires dataFields.

dataConnector.description: The connector whose snapshot subtree this native component's dataFields address, as a slug ("wakatime", "leetcode", "rss"). Absent means "github" — the original native set predates multi-connector natives, so absence defaults rather than requiring every file to say so. Only meaningful with native: true (it qualifies dataFields; loaders enforce that pairing — deliberately not a dependentRequired here so the default-github story stays documented in one place). The renderer passes the generator exactly data[dataConnector]; binding derivation unions dataFields into THIS connector's binding. Community publish validation rejects it along with native/dataFields.

dataFields.description: Connector snapshot paths a native component consumes directly — no {{templates}} involved. Paths are relative to the component's dataConnector subtree and may be dotted ("stats.calendar") or a bare top-level key ("posts" — some snapshots keep a series at the root). Binding derivation unions these into the design's binding for the component's dataConnector (default github) for every instance of the component, so the consent record stays complete.

allOf.$comment: Variant switch on kind (§7.6). kind "code": code required; computed (declarative-only) and the native family (mutually exclusive) forbidden. Any other kind: code forbidden.

Who supplies the render nodes. Native and code components get them from the trusted generator / the sandboxed render function, so declared nodes are only the static palette preview — [] or absent is fine. Declarative components' nodes ARE the component: required, at least one.

propDecl.description: A prop slot: type, optional description, and the default used when an instance omits the prop (and for the palette preview). The default must match the declared type. Color props are strings. "series" props are JSON arrays (a contribution calendar, hours per day, …): at render time an instance value that is a SOLE "{{path}}" template resolves to the RAW array at that path (passed through untouched — never stringified); anything non-array falls back to the declared default with a warning. Declarative fragments do NOT interpolate series values ({{props.x}} of an array resolves to the em-dash placeholder) — only code components (kind "code") consume them in v1.

default.description: The default series — a JSON array; elements are unconstrained JSON (numbers, or objects like {date, count}). It feeds publish validation (code components execute against declared defaults, twice, byte-compared) and palette previews, so make it representative.

fragmentNode.description: Exactly the design-schema node types minus instance — nested instances are rejected in v0.

computedEntry.description: Linear map from a numeric prop onto a node's geometry: node[field] = clamp(props[prop] × scale, clamp[0], clamp[1]), in frame coordinates (instance scaling applies afterwards). Deliberately not an expression language.

node.description: id of a node in this component's nodes

prop.description: name of a declared prop of type number

clamp.description: [min, max] applied after scaling the prop.
